page: Microsoft Azure D64pds_v7 belongs to the general-purpose Dpdsv7 series, delivering 64 dedicated vCPUs using a 64-bit ARM processor architecture. Operating under Microsoft Hyper-V, the system provides 256 GB of system memory, matching an industry-standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM balance with 4.0 GB allocated per virtual core. This configuration omits discrete GPU acceleration, directing all host processing to the ARM CPU infrastructure.

A notable hardware aspect of the D64pds_v7 is its inclusion of 3,780 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage. This direct-attached capacity provides low-latency read and write capabilities, making it effective for temporary storage, fast buffer space, or transient cache files. The instance is capable of attaching premium remote storage for durable requirements, while complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not included by default.

The ARM-based compute architecture yields favorable power and resource efficiency compared to legacy architectures, providing a cost-effective platform for heavily threaded deployments. A primary tradeoff involves binary compatibility, as application stacks must support ARM64 instruction execution. The combination of 64 dedicated cores, 256 GB memory, and high-capacity local NVMe storage positions this server well for container orchestration nodes, multi-tier web hosting, continuous integration runners, and transactional databases requiring extensive local scratch capacity.
description: Microsoft Azure D64pds_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on 64-bit ARM architecture, running under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance provides 64 dedicated vCPUs coupled with 256 GB of system RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 4.0 GB per core. For I/O-intensive workloads, it includes 3,780 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage, offering high-throughput, low-latency scratch space without relying solely on remote network volumes. The configuration contains no dedicated hardware GPUs and includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The ARM64 processor design provides a power-efficient compute model capable of handling high concurrency at lower operational costs compared to traditional x86 alternatives. Given its balanced resource footprint and substantial local high-speed disk capacity, the D64pds_v7 is appropriate for enterprise web serving, microservice architectures, caching tiers, data aggregation pipelines, and relational or NoSQL database workloads requiring quick access to large local caches.
